To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new, versatile, easy, and scalable synthetic method for the preparation of supported Ti-, Al- and Zr-Lewis acid sites in large pore silica.

(i) the use of acetyl acetonates as a stabilizer for the synthesis of mesoporous metalated silica materials is a simple, versatile and efficient approach to prepare large-pore metalated silica materials with well-dispersed metal species, which are active in a wide range of organic reactions, including water-sensitive ones; and (ii) the Lewis acid sites in the metalated silica materials can be quantified and characterized using a combination of Hammett indicator titrations and
we synthesized a series of large pore mesoporous silica materials with supported Lewis acids (Ti-, Al-, Zs) and demonstrated that they can be used as water-tolertant heterogeneous catalysts.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of mesoporous silica materials with supported Lewis acids, which are active catalysts for the direct amidation of electron-deficient and bulky aminophenols and morpholine, even in the presence of water.
the synthesis of water-tolerant supported metal Lewis acids for the direct amidation of electron poor and bulky amino substrates.
a novel synthesis of mesoporous metalated silicates with high concentration of metal centers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Lewis acidity of metalated mesoporous silica materials is strongly dependent on the type of the metal, its concentration and the presence of water, and that the supported metal centers are active catalysts for direct amidation of amines.
the Lewis acidity quantification is a very useful tool in catalyst design and development.
the Ti-SBA-16 catalyst is the best catalyst for the direct amidation reaction of anilines and the Zr-SBA catalyst is the best for morpholine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new class of large pore mesoporous materials with supported Ti, Al and Zr Lewis acids were synthesized, characterized, tested for catalytic activity and compared.

the use of metal-acetylacetonates as precursors for the synthesis of metalated mesoporous silicas is an efficient and versatile approach for the preparation of water-tolerant supported metal centers, with the possibility to control the concentration of the metal species and the Lewis acidity of the solids.
the supported Lewis acids are very active catalysts for the direct amide formation, with high yields, and are tolerant to the presence of water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Lewis acidity of supported metal oxides can be tuned by varying the metal concentration, which is important for the design of efficient supported metal catalysts.
the supported metal oxides can be used as water-tolerance Lewis acids, even in the presence of a large excess of water.
, in the case of Ti-SBA-16, a material with a higher surface area, the catalytic activity was found to be superior to the corresponding Ti-SBA-12.
